name: TN-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans about eleven points Republican and DesJarlais has held it comfortably
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 1 percent
Overwhelming money gap: about $495,000 on hand for the incumbent versus under $9,000 for the Democratic nominee
No public polls or expert ratings; the Democratic-leaning 2026 national climate is the challenger's main source of upside
model.rationale: The district's eleven-point Republican lean, DesJarlais's roughly fifty-to-one cash-on-hand advantage, and market pricing near 1 percent for Democrats leave Broderick without a visible path; even a favorable national environment only trims the incumbent's margin.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against DesJarlais or a fresh scandal could reopen the race, though no such signs have appeared so far.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Scott DesJarlais seeks another term in a Tennessee district that leans about eleven points Republican. He enters the general election having secured his party's nomination with roughly half a million dollars raised and about $495,000 on hand. Democrat Victoria Broderick has raised under $85,000 and reported fewer than $9,000 in the bank, and two independents on the ballot show negligible fundraising. Prediction markets give Democrats about a 1 percent chance of an upset.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on the district's lean, the money gap, and market pricing. The 2026 national climate leans toward Democrats and could narrow the margin somewhat, but a deficit of this size in territory this red leaves the incumbent clearly favored. The main question is the size of the Republican win, not the winner.
